Gojo vs Raycast: MacBook notch controls or a keyboard-first launcher?

Raycast is a keyboard-first command interface and extension hub. Gojo is a hoverable notch surface for controls you want to see and touch quickly.

Updated July 8, 20266 min readAll posts

Short answer

Choose Raycast if your workflow begins with a keyboard shortcut, search, commands, extensions, snippets, and automation across apps and services. Choose Gojo if you prefer a hoverable MacBook-notch surface for glanceable controls such as media, windows, clipboard, files, calendar, battery, webcam, and Night Shift.

  • Best specialist fit: keyboard-first commands, search, extensions, snippets, and app automation.
  • Best Gojo fit: pointer-friendly, glanceable controls that live near the MacBook notch.
  • Use both if Raycast runs command workflows and Gojo handles quick visual controls.
On this page Comparison table Where each app fits Permission notes FAQ

Comparison table

AppPrimary jobBest fitGojo angle
RaycastKeyboard-first launcher and command interfacePeople who want to search, launch, automate, and use extensions without leaving the keyboardGojo favors hoverable, glanceable access in the MacBook notch.
RaycastKeyboard window managementUsers who want configurable hotkeys and layoutsGojo provides window snapping inside a wider notch utility.
RaycastExtensible productivity hubUsers who need integrations, scripts, snippets, and command workflowsGojo stays focused on a compact set of built-in MacBook controls.
GojoMulti-tool notch surfaceUsers who want immediate access near the menu bar and camera areaA complement to Raycast’s command-palette workflow.

Where each app fits

Where Raycast is stronger

Raycast is stronger when the keyboard is the center of the workflow. It is built for launching, searching, commands, snippets, AI, extensions, and configurable actions.

Where Gojo is stronger

Gojo is stronger when the interaction should be visual and close to the notch. It keeps media, windows, clipboard, files, calendar, battery, webcam, and display controls in a compact surface.

When to use both

Use Raycast for keyboard-first commands and integrations, then use Gojo for quick visual or pointer-accessible controls in the notch.

Permissions and trust notes

Comparison pages are only useful if they are honest about scope. Gojo is a MacBook notch utility, not a blanket replacement for every specialist app. Before granting macOS Accessibility, Automation, Camera, Calendar, or other permissions to any utility, check whether the requested access matches the feature you plan to use.

Official sources checked for this page on July 8, 2026: Raycast official site, Raycast manual, Raycast window management

  • Raycast positions itself as a shortcut to everything and an extendable launcher.
  • Raycast documents launching apps, searching files, managing windows, snippets, AI, extensions, and third-party integrations.
  • Raycast documents keyboard-driven window commands, custom commands, and layouts.

Comparison method: recommendations are based on primary workflow, permission fit, official source claims, and whether Gojo should complement or replace the specialist app.

FAQ

Is Gojo a Raycast replacement?

No. Raycast is an extensible keyboard-first launcher and command interface. Gojo is a MacBook-notch control surface with a more focused built-in utility set.

Do Gojo and Raycast both manage windows?

Yes. Raycast offers keyboard-driven window movement, resizing, custom commands, and layouts. Gojo includes window snapping as one notch control.

Can Gojo and Raycast run together?

Yes. Raycast centers on keyboard commands, while Gojo centers on a hoverable MacBook notch. Check and adjust shortcuts if your configuration overlaps.

Which is better for clipboard history?

Raycast includes clipboard history as part of its launcher feature set. Gojo includes clipboard history for people who want that access inside the notch.
